title: David Ellison’s Vision for CNN: Same C.E.O and No Bari Weiss, for Now.
partialText: David Ellison is negotiating to keep CNN’s chief executive, Mark Thompson, in place without oversight from Bari Weiss, the CBS editor in chief, when the networks’ parent companies merge.

title: US Sanctions A7, a Russia Firm That Helps Sidestep Economic Restrictions
partialText: The move follows recent reports detailing how A7, a Russian financial firm, used shell companies around the world to move funds on behalf of restricted Russian businesses.

title: What to Know About Trump Accounts as More Than 60 Million Children Are Auto-Enrolled
partialText: The Trump administration may have just signed up your child — and more than 60 million others — for a 530A savings account (if you haven’t already done so).

title: Swedish Company Uses A.I. Likeness of Greta Garbo in Ad
partialText: An ad produced by the manufacturing company SKF Group featured a digital version of the Swedish American actress, who died in 1990. Not all viewers found the replica convincing.

title: As Mortgage Rates Hit Highest Level Since 2023, Buyers Look at ARMs
partialText: The average 30-year, fixed-rate home loan rose to 7.28 percent, up from 6.34 percent a year ago. More buyers are now turning to adjustable-rate mortgages.

title: Trump’s Threat to Ban Diesel Exports Sets Off Global Alarms
partialText: A reduction in refineries has already driven the price of diesel to record highs, threatening economies. An U.S. export ban would be “tremendous shock and blow.”

title: Federal Watchdog Investigates Adam Kinzinger for Kalshi Bets on His Pardon
partialText: The inquiry by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission centers on bets the former congressman made on Kalshi in the weeks before he was pardoned in January 2025.

title: U.S. Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
partialText: The higher yields, which are pressuring consumer and corporate borrowers and increasingly weighing on certain corners of the stock market, are unlikely to dissipate soon.

title: The Global Bond Rout Reaches Worrying New Levels
partialText: Investors are on alert as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note hit a new multi-decade high. The sell-off is also broadening in Europe, too.

title: Oil Is Flowing From the Persian Gulf, but Prices Remain High. Why?
partialText: Crude oil costs close to $100 a barrel because traders are worried hostilities could soon restart and the world is burning through its emergency stockpiles.

title: How Middle East Oil Exports Started Recovering
partialText: Our business reporter Peter Eavis describes how oil exports from the Middle East have rebounded this month, getting closer to the levels seen before the Iran war.

title: When Data Centers Cluster Together, How Dirty Are They? One County Wants Answers.
partialText: An unusual study aims to estimate the pollution and health costs from a cluster of proposed data centers, instead of considering each one separately.

title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
partialText: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.

title: Help! Air Canada Got Me to Europe, Then Stranded Me There.
partialText: The airline helpfully rebooked a delayed traveler from Toronto, but failed to mention it had also canceled her return trip. She spent $800 to get home.

title: New York Times Reporting Through a Front Page That Never Published and More
partialText: Times reporters and editors discuss items that have shaped our coverage, including Dean Baquet on the “Madam President” front page that never was.

title: Bessent Settled Tax Issue That Had Put Him at Odds With I.R.S.
partialText: The Treasury Secretary had previously taken a position on his taxes that contradicted the views of the tax agency that he now oversees.

title: Trump Dangles Alaska Gas Project as Part of Korean Investment Package
partialText: The long-delayed project, which the developer has not yet formally greenlit, would deliver Alaskan gas to Asian markets but take several years to construct.

title: Mattel Chief Named Co-C.E.O. of Combined Paramount and Warner Bros.
partialText: Ynon Kreiz, who will work alongside David Ellison at the merged company, helped turn Barbie into a blockbuster movie.

title: While Surging to Records, Stocks Experience Some ‘Wobbles’
partialText: Beneath the S&P 500’s 2 percent gain in the third quarter, the rise in oil prices and bond yields led some investors to become more cautious about the outlook for A.I. profits.

title: Trump Media’s Merger With Nuclear Fusion Company Moves Closer to Completion
partialText: A securities filing laid out the terms of the deal between Truth Social’s parent company and TAE Technologies, which was formally announced in December.

title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
partialText: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.

title: E.E.O.C. Sues Harvard for Data on Diversity in Hiring Practices
partialText: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filed a lawsuit asking a judge to compel the university to provide information on hiring practices that the agency said discriminated against white men.

title: Google Wants Hollywood to Stop Being So Afraid of Technology
partialText: 100 Zeros, a collaboration between Google and Range Media Partners, aims to give the tech giant a foothold in movies, TV and emerging forms of entertainment.

title: Medical Records Firm Uses AI Tool to Expose Flaws that Threaten Patient Privacy
partialText: Epic’s engineers deployed an Anthropic tool that exposed security risks that could allow undetected access to millions of patient records.

title: Condé Nast C.E.O. Leaves to Run Mattel
partialText: Roger Lynch, who has led the publisher for more than seven years, will become the chief executive of the toy company, he said Wednesday.

title: Fed’s Preferred Inflation Gauge Points to Continued Price Pressures
partialText: The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index showed little sign of easing in August, though revised data showed inflation had been slightly cooler than previously believed.

title: Bracing for More Inflation Volatility
partialText: Consumers, business owners and investors are growing increasingly concerned about rising inflation, and its potential repercussions.

title: DeepSeek and Huawei Target a Key Source of Nvidia’s A.I. Dominance
partialText: In China’s push for self-reliance in artificial intelligence, DeepSeek and Huawei have teamed up to develop software tools for advanced chips.

title: Trump’s New Tariffs Get a Familiar Day in Court
partialText: For the third time in less than two years, the Trump administration returned to court on Wednesday to defend its power to wage a punishing global trade war.

title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid
partialText: Streaming services can introduce you to a wonderland of nearly unlimited audio, but downloading your digital collection has advantages.

title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley
partialText: Bill Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, when the Santa Clara Valley was better known for apricot orchards than microchips. He has died at 98.

title: Troubles at Situational Awareness Point to Record Stock Market Leverage
partialText: A meltdown at Situational Awareness, an A.I.-focused investment firm, is raising tough questions about the Wall Street banks that lent billions to the upstart firm.

title: A.I. Is ‘Better Informed’ Than Doctors, Kennedy Tells Industry-Backed MAHA Summit
partialText: The health secretary, Vice President JD Vance and other top officials addressed a conference sponsored by corporations, including A.I. companies and others with business before the government.

title: X2, Troubled Six Flags Roller Coaster, to Close After Lawsuits
partialText: The ride at Magic Mountain near Los Angeles has fueled lawsuits claiming that it had caused brain injuries, including two that were fatal.

title: Paramount’s Streaming Chief Leaves Ahead of Warner Bros. Deal
partialText: Cindy Holland’s departure clears the way for Casey Bloys, the HBO chairman, to have a leading role in the combined company’s streaming services.

title: Tankers Are Loading Oil Again From a Vital Saudi Pipeline
partialText: Saudi authorities had taken the pipeline offline this month after it was damaged in a drone attack by an Iranian-backed Iraqi militia.

title: Black Voting Groups Prepare for Disinformation Campaigns in the Midterms
partialText: A new “propaganda playbook” aims to demystify common techniques used to target Black Americans, long a powerful voting bloc, with election-related disinformation.

title: Trump Administration Prepares to Ask Tax Filers if They Are U.S. Citizens
partialText: The new question, included on a draft version of the primary tax form, comes as part of an anti-immigrant turn at an agency that long prioritized tax administration.

title: Sunkist Fruit Gems, Bar Mitzvah Staple, Get 2nd Chance After Discontinuation
partialText: The company said that Candyrific of Louisville, Ky., will produce the jelly candy that comes in a rainbow of colors and citrus flavors and is used in Jewish traditions.

title: What’s In Anthropic’s I.P.O. Filing
partialText: The artificial intelligence giant reportedly believes that it’s on track for a record-breaking stock market listing, according to a prospectus seen by Reuters.

title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
partialText: Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.

title: Mideast Oil Exports Rebound Even as Prices Remain Elevated
partialText: More tankers are moving through the Strait of Hormuz as shippers gain confidence, but the global supply of oil is still below demand.

title: US Hits Canada With Ban on Some Dairy and Liquor Products
partialText: An outright ban on certain Canadian products took effect Tuesday, escalating a damaging trade fight between the two North American allies.

title: For Japan’s Young Singles, Romance Gets a Corporate Middleman
partialText: A generation exhausted by dating apps is embracing a corporate reinvention of traditional matchmaking, fueling an industry that promises a fast track to marriage.

title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico Seek a Longer Reprieve From White House Ban
partialText: A federal court temporarily lifted the ban last week. The outlets want a longer pause while they sue to restore their access.

title: Could Homeownership Reverse the Decline in Birthrates?
partialText: Researchers looked back at the baby-boom era and found that federal mortgage programs played a part in the country’s population upswing after World War II.

title: Two of China’s EV Makers Announce a Deal as Auto Industry Moves Toward Consolidation
partialText: Two of the country’s leading makers of electric vehicles announced they are merging their battery swapping and charging operations.

title: Nvidia Adds $150 Billion to Massive Stock Buyback, the Largest Ever
partialText: The increase comes four months after the chip giant added $80 billion to its buyback program, bringing the total remaining authorized amount to $235 billion.

title: Could A.I. Safety Risks Derail the Sector’s I.P.O. Prospects?
partialText: Big liability questions lie ahead for the artificial intelligence labs Anthropic and OpenAI as they push ahead with plans to go public.
